Use `app.dependency_overrides` to replace the dependency with a fake that returns a mock value. Your FastAPI application has an attribute `app.dependency_overrides`, it is a simple `dict`.[2] To override a dependency for testing, you put as a key the original dependency (a function), and as the value, your dependency override (another function).[2] And then FastAPI will call that override instead of the original dependency.[2]

This fits your case. The docs give the example of an external provider that might be charging you per request[1]. In that situation, you can override the dependency that calls that provider, and use a custom dependency that returns a mock user, only for your tests.[1] The original dependency won't run (nor any of the sub-dependencies it might have).[1]

Here's the pattern from the docs:

```python
client = TestClient(app)

async def override_dependency(q: str | None = None):
    return {"q": q, "skip": 5, "limit": 10}

app.dependency_overrides[common_parameters] = override_dependency

def test_override_in_items():
    response = client.get("/items/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
```

In your code, use your API-calling dependency as the key and a function returning fake data as the value.

**Resetting overrides:** you can reset your overrides (remove them) by setting `app.dependency_overrides` to be an empty `dict`[2]:

```python
app.dependency_overrides = {}
```

If you want to override a dependency only during some tests, you can set the override at the beginning of the test (inside the test function) and reset it at the end (at the end of the test function).[2]
